task.title: Configuring federation audiences
task.shortdesc: To manage robot federation entries in Red Hat Quay, you can use the robot federation API to set the issuer and subject that map an OIDC identity to a robot account.

ul.li: You have created an organization and robot account.
You have configured OIDC for your Red Hat Quay deployment.
You have the issuer URL and subject identifier from your OIDC provider.

context.p: Each robot federation entry maps an external OIDC identity (issuer and subject) to a Red Hat Quay robot account. Starting in Red Hat Quay 3.18, robot federation supports an optional audiences array on each entry for token audience validation during federated robot token exchange (GET /oauth2/federation/robot/token).

note.p: In Red Hat Quay 3.18, create and update requests persist issuer and subject only. The optional audiences field is not stored from API requests, and the Red Hat Quay v2 UI federation modal does not provide an audiences field. Until API support is available, federated robot token exchange skips audience validation and logs a deprecation warning when audiences is not stored for the matching federation entry. A later release requires audiences for federated robot authentication.

context.p: When audiences is present in stored federation configuration, configure it to match the aud claim values your OIDC provider issues—for example, a custom API audience such as api://quay-api for Microsoft Entra ID v2.0 tokens, or your OIDC client ID for standard flows. For Microsoft Entra ID v2.0, use an application-specific audience rather than the Microsoft Graph audience.
